purpose: External Lean library import allowlist. Release-candidate deliverables may import only packages listed here with status ACTIVE or PROBATIONARY; this registry is not a mathematical-correctness certification.

policy.pin_rule: Each project pins full commits in lake-manifest.json. This registry records policy and rationale; it never floats a version at build time.
policy.toolchain_rule: Record the actual toolchain and mathlib rev before first use, after an import smoke test.
policy.revocation_rule: Revoking an entry blocks new builds using it; historical records keep their original environment attribution.
policy.approval_rule: Single maintainer: every entry must carry rationale and approved_at. No second reviewer exists, so entries must stay machine-checkable and honest.
policy.enforcement: Not yet enforced by check_interfaces.py; import-versus-registry consistency is a declared open item.

packages.name: mathlib
packages.rationale: Community-mainline mathematics library with maintainer review and CI. Already used at full-commit pins by the formal/ Lean projects and audited under Audit.lean.
known_risks: Trust is transitive: the manifest pulls in aesop, batteries, Qq, plausible, proofwidgets, importGraph, LeanSearchClient and Cli at pinned revs.
Reproduction must consume manifest resolved revs, never re-resolve inputRev values such as main.

packages.name: physlib
packages.rationale: Community physics library (formed by merging PhysLean/HepLean with Lean-QuantumInfo in March 2026, now under leanprover-community). First registry version admits the reviewed Physlib core target only. Status stays PROBATIONARY: admitted in policy, blocked in practice until the toolchain conflict in known_risks is resolved and an import smoke test with `#print axioms` is recorded in pinned_rev_examples.
import_restrictions: Only the reviewed Physlib core target is admitted by default. PhyslibAlpha accepts large-scale AI contributions under a lighter review process and requires a separate decision; the QuantumInfo target has its own conventions and is not auto-admitted.

ENFORCEMENT CAVEAT: defaultTargets in physlib's lakefile only controls what a bare `lake build` builds INSIDE physlib. It places no restriction on downstream imports -- PhyslibAlpha is a declared lean_lib, so `import PhyslibAlpha.X` from this repository would simply work. This restriction must be enforced by our own import scanner and is currently a declared open item, not a guarantee.
known_risks: SORRY WARNINGS ARE DISABLED UPSTREAM: all three lean_libs (Physlib, PhyslibAlpha, QuantumInfo) set -Dwarn.sorry=false, so physlib deliberately contains sorry and suppresses the warning. A theorem of ours importing a physlib lemma can therefore report sorryAx under `#print axioms`, which is a hard failure against our allow-list {propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound}. Run `#print axioms` on every target after any physlib import; this is the CONFORMANCE E06 scenario and it is expected, not hypothetical.

VERIFIED INCOMPATIBLE with the current environment, not merely unverified: physlib pins leanprover/lean4:v4.33.0 and mathlib v4.33.0, while formal/ is pinned to leanprover/lean4:v4.30.0-rc2 with mathlib c1e30e172c8fda21e6776bf1f10351e882ee31b9. A lake project has exactly one toolchain and one mathlib, so physlib cannot be added without upgrading the whole chain and re-running every affected check per REVIEW section 6 (all three formal/ projects lose their current pass).
Importing physlib drags doc-gen4 (a documentation generator) into the dependency closure; trust is transitive and this widens the surface beyond mathematics.
Actively evolving; upgrades may break downstream. Handle per REVIEW section 6 environment-change rules.

upstream_observed.source: https://github.com/leanprover-community/physlib master lakefile.toml and lean-toolchain, read directly
upstream_observed.mathlib_pin_style: TAG, not a full commit. This conflicts with this registry's pin_rule; the real pin must be read from physlib's own lake-manifest.json, never from its lakefile.
